READ_THIS_FIRST: A verdict is sound ONLY for a producer QOU_Q0_ANCHOR actually reaches. The reachability test was WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS in the first version and the count hid it: bare-name matching gave 15 of 21 on 2026-08-29, the corrected test also gives 15, over a DIFFERENT SET. It falsely refused rho_f_categorical_probe (names the producer in a docstring, never reads the witness) and falsely RAN qbeta_jacobi_anger_tower_general (reaches muon via q_muon_at(), never mentions the file) — the second being a false pass, the dangerous direction. A matching count is not agreement.

hadron_knot_table.detail: exceeded 7200s. NOT a pass and NOT a fail: it does not establish whether the producer works at the proton pin. It DOES establish a measured lower bound, and a much stronger one than AGENTS.md carries. The three A=1 atoms (proton, neutron, protium) were all complete by the FIRST 30s progress tick; the log then never grew again across 239 further ticks. So deuterium -- atom 4 of 19, the first BOUND atom -- ran >=7170s (~2h) without finishing, against the ~50 min AGENTS.md records before its own timeout cut it off. Producer held 100% CPU throughout (7196s cpu / 7190s wall, RSS 611 MB), so this is compute, not a stall.

reachability.no_live_producer_note: alpha_high_precision is listed in ideal_muon but its ONLY file on main is computations/_deprecated/alpha_high_precision.py. The check tool's SKIP tuple excludes _deprecated, so this stem is neither A nor B: there is no live producer to run at either pin. It is a manifest entry with nothing behind it. Do NOT count it as an unmeasured group-A hold. Measured 2026-08-30 by rglob over computations/ with SKIP applied; an rglob WITHOUT SKIP puts it in A_measurable and inflates that list to 4 — that is the deprecated file being read as live, not a fourth measurable producer.

physical_proton.why: q_parameter's default for an unlisted stem is already proton, so this entry changes no behaviour for any file, live or deprecated. Removing it would be a true no-op; kept for symmetry with the ideal_muon case, which is not.

reachability.tranche_note:
UPDATED 2026-09-03 (bean qou-aj91). Two changes moved these lists, and they are different in kind -- do not conflate them.
(1) ROUTING. Nine producers were routed through q_parameter, so QOU_Q0_ANCHOR now reaches them. All nine stay listed ideal_muon except cross_check_trM_cw_seminormal_leg, which moved to physical_proton because its reference witness is proton-stamped. q_parameter derives the muon anchor from q_muon_at(70), byte-identical to 70 digits with what the direct reads returned, so routing moved no number.
(2) DETECTOR FIX. env_override_reaches() had keyed on the witness FILENAME, which cannot tell reading a file from mentioning it: it matched routing comments, add_upstream() provenance edges, and a witness string describing history, and so reported all nine routed producers as still bypassed. It now keys on derived_50_digit -- the field a value-read always subscripts -- over comment- and docstring-stripped source. Verified 15/15 against the 9 routed and the 6 exclusions before adoption.
So A 3 -> 11 and B 15 -> 6, and part of that movement is producers being fixed while part is the detector stopping lying about them.
reachability.B_is_now_exclusions_only: All 6 remaining B entries are PRINCIPLED exclusions, not backlog: q_pinning_50_digit defines the anchor; q0_anchor_consistency_audit is the flip detector and needs both pins; cross_check_trM_1ppb's own source requires muon; atomic_tr_m_mpfr_50dps is dual-layer and asserts BOTH pins; qbeta_jacobi_anger_tower_general deliberately compares both (anchors = {'proton': q_at(), 'muon': q_muon_at()}); q1_mass_gap_probe validates two_q and plancherel_weights_n3 from the SAME witness, values derived at its own q0, so routing q0 away while keeping those comparisons would manufacture a straddle. Nothing is left in B by accident.
